Signs of the World

Two way traffic ahead

History

The 1968 Vienna Convention on Road Signs and Signals recommends opposing arrows, repeated along the stretch as often as needed, and reversed in countries that drive on the left.

Adoption

The Vienna Convention specifies two warning shapes. Most of Europe uses triangles. The United States, Canada, Mexico, Australia, Japan, New Zealand and most of Central and South America use diamonds.
